title: Your real conversation, your story, your next 90 days

say: Your real conversation, your story, your next 90 days.
This is the video for Module 4 of Communication and Self-Expression: portfolio and impact.
In this module you take one real situation from your life and prepare it the way a professional prepares an important meeting. Preparation does not make you sound rehearsed. It frees you to listen.

say: During the talk, paraphrase before you answer, say your request once, then pause. Close by summarising who does what and by when.
Within 24 hours, reflect. What happened? Then, so what? What does it show about your skills, and where did you slide into passive or aggressive?

left: What it shows about my skills
right: What I will do next time
The next step with this person

say: Then, now what? What will you do next time? If it went badly, an honest reflection is still excellent evidence. Learning is the goal, not a perfect result.

say: For example, Aisha in Kano used to say, I'm just a small trader. Now she starts with the present: her name and what she does, in plain words. No apology first.

cards.d: 'I'm Aisha Bello. I sell Ankara and lace fabrics from my stall in Kantin Kwari market.'
'I started eight years ago with one bale. About half my sales are regular customers.'
'This year I want to supply tailors in bulk. If you know one, let's talk after.'

say: Then the past: one or two facts that explain her experience. She started eight years ago with one bale.

cards.d: 'I'm Aisha Bello. I sell Ankara and lace fabrics from my stall in Kantin Kwari market.'
'I started eight years ago with one bale. About half my sales are regular customers.'
'This year I want to supply tailors in bulk. If you know one, let's talk after.'

say: Then the future, with a link to the listeners. This year I want to supply tailors in bulk. Two tailors approached her after the meeting.
60 seconds is about 120 to 150 spoken words, so time yourself and trim.

say: Gather everything in one place. Re-score your ten situations without looking at your old scores. For example, Funmi went from 28 to 36 out of 50, and explains it with her journal.
Some scores may stay the same. That honesty strengthens your portfolio. Store it privately, and use first names or initials only.

say: Plan your next 90 days in three stages: practise, stretch, then review and teach a friend. Keep each weekly action small, and check in with a practice partner every two weeks. If you miss a week, restart without punishing yourself.
Continue with the lessons below.
